title: sparse-label-reconciliation-pulse-notebook
content:
Personal scratchpad — sparse label reconciliation
Purpose:
- Capture quick heuristics and examples for harmonizing checkbox/multi-select/single-select fields with lots of nulls or sentinel values.
- Draft QA sampling and adjudication rules that we can try in the next cleanup sprint.
- Record unresolved questions for triage in the weekly DL sync.

Context / why this hurts:
- Many datasets have a user-supplied field (e.g., 'marketing_consent', 'contact_opt_in', 'product_preferences') where ~60-85% are blank or use freeform answers like 'N/A', 'nope', 'opted out', '0'.
- Downstream model features assume clean binary/multi-hot vectors. Naive casting (blank -> 0) biases both precision and recall and hides systematic missingness.

High-level reconciliation approach (working rules):
1) Normalize first: strip whitespace, lowercase, remove punctuation except relevant +/-, collapse long whitespace.
2) Map common synonyms/variants with small lemmatized dictionary: yes/true/y/1/opted in -> POSITIVE; no/false/n/0/opted out/decline -> NEGATIVE.
3) Treat explicit 'prefer not to say' and 'no answer' as ABSTAIN (separate code), not negative.
4) Blank vs explicit null/sentinel: keep blank as MISSING (do not automatically impute). If pipeline requires a value, map MISSING -> ABSTAIN for evaluation, but keep original MISSING flag for downstream analyses.
5) Multi-value parsing: split on common separators (comma, semicolon, |, /) but respect quoted commas. If split results in any POSITIVE token -> mark that option positive.
6) Numeric fields with 0/1: confirm source contract (some older exports used 0=unspecified). If metadata unavailable, sample 300 rows randomly to estimate mapping.
7) Low-frequency tokens (<0.1%): route to human review sample; try fuzzy match to known tokens (Levenshtein <=2) before falling back to REVIEW.

Examples (raw -> recommended normalized tags):
- "" (empty string) -> MISSING
- "N/A" or "na" -> ABSTAIN
- "No, thanks" -> NEGATIVE
- "Yes, please!" -> POSITIVE
- "opted out; do not email" -> NEGATIVE
- "1" (context: contact_opt_in) -> POSITIVE (after verifying origin)
- "0" (same field) -> NEGATIVE (if we confirm binary contract)
- "prefer not to answer" -> ABSTAIN
- "email,sms" (multi-select) -> {email: POSITIVE, sms: POSITIVE} (other channels MISSING)
- "none" -> NEGATIVE (but watch for 'none of the above' vs 'none specified')

QA sampling strategy (proposed):
- Stratified sample of 800 rows across: 1) explicit POS/NEG, 2) ABSTAIN tokens, 3) BLANK/MISSING, 4) low-frequency tokens, 5) numeric-only records.
- Aim for at least: 200 ABSTAIN/NA examples, 200 blank, 200 low-freq, 200 numeric/ambiguous.
- Each sample labeled by 2 annotators; disagreements -> adjudicator. Track confusion matrix.

Adjudication rules (quick):
- If annotator labels differ between POSITIVE vs NEGATIVE and one tag is ABSTAIN, prefer ABSTAIN only if both indicate uncertainty language; otherwise prefer explicit sentiment.
- When one annotator marks REVIEW because of ambiguous context (e.g., asking about future consent), escalate.

Pipeline checks and unit tests to add:
- Normalization roundtrip test: random subset normalized -> reformat to canonical -> verify fuzzy match score > 0.95 against known dictionary.
- Separator edgecases: inputs with embedded commas in quotes should not be split. Add tests with 10 patterns.
- Blank handling: ensure blank != 'n/a' != 'none' in canonicalized output.
- Frequency drift alert: daily job to report any token whose frequency increases by >5x week-over-week.

Edge cases / weird examples to watch for:
- Multilingual inputs ("sí", "oui", "ja") — mapping table missing for many languages; fallback is REVIEW.
- Hyphenated tokens where dash implies range or negation ("no-email/text") — need regex to detect compound negatives.
- Transcribed responses where punctuation removal loses 'no.' vs 'no' ambiguous.
- Emojis used as consent markers (thumbs up / thumbs down) — capture with emoji map.

Operational notes for labeling tool (for annotators):
- Provide short context snippet: source field name, export date, any UX copy shown to user at time of input.
- Add quick hint: 'If user typed something clearly like "no", choose NEGATIVE. If they typed "N/A" or "prefer not", choose ABSTAIN.'
- One-click actions for common maps (Yes -> POS, No -> NEG, N/A -> ABSTAIN).

Open questions / things to resolve in triage:
- Should we represent ABSTAIN as a separate feature in downstream models or collapse with MISSING? (impact on cal metric).
- How to handle platform-specific sentinel values (some exports use "-1" meaning not shown vs explicitly declined). Need mapping table per-exporter.
- Which rare languages do we support with quick dictionary vs send to human review? Prioritize Spanish, French, Portuguese, German, Japanese.

Next steps (owners + rough ETA):
- Diego: build normalization lib PR with emoji + multilingual short map (due 2025-02-14).
- Priya: prepare stratified QA sample export and annotation job (due 2025-02-10).
- Liam: add drift alert dashboard prototype to console-data (due 2025-02-21).
- Me (Amina): compile adjudicator rubric and one-pager for annotators (due 2025-02-07).

Notes to self: keep this lightweight. Iterate after first 2 sprints and fold frequent new sentinels into normalization table. Capture one concrete dataset case study (marketing_consent_2024Q4) for the docs.

Quick references:
- DL ticket: DL-4721 (schema mismatch and sentinel values)
- Working PR: github.com/redwood-inference/labeling-utils/pull/214 (starter normalizer)
- Slack: #data-labeling pinned message "consent-sentinels"

End of scratchpad.
